_comment: Each test's verdict from the very deep check's TEST WORTH section (practice: very-deep-check, Pass 2's question 27; tools/test_review.py reads this file).

verdicts: test name (a harness check_* function, or a test script's path) -> {verdict, importance, why, date, by, seconds, leads}. verdict is keep, cheapen or retire. A keep says its importance: high (work lost, leaked, landed in the wrong place, or a session blocked), medium (a mechanism quietly wrong), low (wording, formatting, a convenience). seconds is the recorded time when judged, and leads the leads it carried then: a keep is judged again when its time more than doubles, or a new lead appears. cheapen and retire are owed in the same pass; a cheapened test is recorded again as keep with its new time, and a retired test is deleted with its entry.
by: "agent" for the session's own call; a person's name, with strength (decided or assented), when the person decided it (practice: decision-strength).

retired: things that are gone, with the patterns a test that still exercises them would contain. A test naming one is a lead for the session, never a verdict: a test OF the retirement names it on purpose. tools/our_language.json's retired words, decommissioned tools/ paths and retired or deduplicated practices are read as well, so they are not repeated here.

Cheapened 2026-10-31: when every case runs, the baseline is a --full-sweep and the 85 or so cases with no setup=, extra= or env_extra= read their clean verdict from it instead of copying the tree and starting an interpreter each; a slug the sweep does not show clean, or output it cannot attribute, is re-checked on its own copy as before. Proved with a check broken to fire on a clean tree (caught by its control and the baseline) and one broken never to fire (caught by its planted case). Back to back on a quiet machine: 329.4 s before, 327.3 s after -- the CPU saved (446.9 to 384.0 s with other work on the cores) does not shorten the wall time, because the main thread runs about 44 extra --only checks and 50 tree copies one after another and reads many cases back right after starting them. Making those run side by side is the next real saving, and a larger edit than this pass.

check_push_destination_reaches_the_views.why: Push check learns the destination branch so a set's commits are held to that rung.

check_universal_change_names_the_set_cop.why: A universal practice change names set copies that override it; awareness note.

check_update_fetches_brought_sets_before.why: Update fetches brought sets before syncing views; otherwise the sync drops the absent sets' practices.

check_freshness_reads_a_section0_catalog.why: Freshness reads a section 0 catalogue by its CATALOGUE_SYNC.json instead of reporting 159 practices absent every session.

check_update_asks_headings_only_of_publi.why: View migration asks for headline case only on files title_case would judge; noise.

check_vocabulary_reads_a_materialized_pr.why: Vocabulary does not call a materialized practice 'defined twice'; false-positive guard.

check_vocabulary_scan_skips_code_owner_c.why: Very deep check's spoken-command list leaves out code-owner-only commands, as the vocabulary page does.

check_spoken_commands_lead_the_session_s.why: Spoken commands come before the cut in a multi-repo session's start output; otherwise the stage words never reach the session.

check_citations_skip_a_generated_block.why: Update's citation list skips generated blocks the repo cannot edit; noise.

check_citations_in_a_declared_record_are.why: Update's citation list skips declared records; noise.

check_update_adopts_an_earlier_runs_cata.why: A rerun stages an earlier run's catalogue mirror when it matches upstream; otherwise 80 files sat unstaged beside a manifest naming the new commit.

check_set_words_leave_out_the_set_itself.why: set_words leaves the set itself out in a worktree, which --run-tests uses; otherwise a set's own words refuse its own text.

check_moves_core_names_exist_in_the_engi.why: Every MOVES_CORE name exists in precedent_branches; a rename otherwise breaks Promote in every repo.

check_bound_set_tools_and_reply_examples.why: Undeclared engine calls by bound set tools and reply examples are held in any repo.

check_set_words_hold_a_practice_printed_.why: set_words holds a practice's printed parts to the set's output patterns.

check_resolver_leaves_out_the_set_itself.why: declared_source_paths leaves the repo itself out by name, not only path; otherwise a set loads itself twice.

check_a_missing_clone_says_not_cloned.why: Reads 'not cloned at <path>' rather than 'no practices/'; diagnostic wording.

check_refresh_refuses_an_untested_main.why: A bare refresh following main refuses a tip whose GitHub test is running or failed; otherwise a broken engine reaches every consumer.

check_codeowners_stamp_hashes_only_the_r.why: CODEOWNERS stamp hashes only its registry; avoids a false stale report.

check_planted_sweep_runs_only_in_a_named.why: The planted-case sweep runs only in named whole-suite runs; keeps quick tiers quick without dropping it from the nightly.

check_a_landing_names_the_checks_it_reac.why: After a staging landing the land tool prints the background harness command; guidance.

check_as_ci_says_why_a_shard_failed.why: --as-ci prints a failed shard's FAIL lines and stderr tail; diagnostic.

check_very_deep_check_registers_its_own_.why: Very deep check registers its record files in generated_files.json once each.

check_branch_policy_seam_asks_a_set_and_.why: Branch policy seam decides tiers, push check depth and whether work reaches main only by Promote; wrong answers land work in the wrong place.

check_summary_fields_drop_links_before_t.why: summary_text.py drops links before cutting a one-line field; avoids half-links.

check_title_case_knows_the_files_it_ship.why: title_case classifies every root file the project instantiates; heading style scope.

check_template_freshness_reads_the_skele.why: Very deep check's reverse skeleton check invents no gaps; report precision.

check_due_reminder_reaches_the_reply.why: build_todo_index.remind() puts due reminders in the reply gate (todo-reminder); a missed reminder is a dropped commitment.

check_todo_and_gotcha_sweeps.why: very_deep_check's open-item sweep and gotcha-retirement candidates against planted fixtures.

check_update_leftovers_installs_and_stam.why: Four update answers consumers' landings depended on (left-for-you on removed checks, installs, stamps).

bridge/tests/test_chatbridge.py.why: Unit and end-to-end tests of the Telegram chat bridge, a test build still in the tree and indexed in WHERE_THINGS_ARE.md; its guard keeps machinery unchangeable from chat. Not timed; about 3 s wall locally.

local/tools/checks/tests/test_install_de.why: Tests check_install_declares_its_scope.py, which precedent_check.py --list still runs for the active local practice install-declares-its-scope.

local/tools/checks/tests/test_park_it.sh.why: Tests check_park_it.py, still run by precedent_check.py and cited by universal park-it and very-deep-check, although local/practices/park-it.md is itself deduplicated.

local/tools/checks/tests/test_philosophy.why: Tests the two philosophy/ checks, both still run for active local practices.

check_test_review_times_script_tests.why: Added 2026-10-31 with the mechanism it tests: without it a practice set's script tests carry no time, and the rule that re-judges a keep whose time more than doubled can never fire for them.

check_no_fixture_points_git_config_at_de.why: Refuses os.devnull or /dev/null as git's global or system config anywhere under tools/: one git config --global under it replaces the container's null device (2026-10-10, 2026-10-31).
